content.title: Christianity & Hinduism
content.subtitle: The self, action and the invitation to refuge.
content.description: A focused encounter with the Bhagavad Gita: the enduring self, action and refuge in Krishna. This devotional reading is a starting point; ask which texts and interpretations your neighbour trusts.

christian.text: Christian hope is bodily resurrection: what is sown perishable is raised imperishable.

other.text: Gita 2.20 describes the self as unborn and enduring, surviving the destruction of the body.

rows.question: How should we understand our works?

christian.text: We are saved by grace through faith and created in Christ for good works.

other.text: Gita 2.47 urges action without claiming its fruits, while also rejecting attachment to inaction.

rows.question: In whom do we take refuge?

christian.text: Jesus invites the burdened to come to him for rest.

other.text: In Gita 18.66 Krishna calls Arjuna to take refuge in him and promises release from sin. Shared language invites careful comparison of who offers deliverance.

reviews.scope: Comparison claims, primary texts, Scripture references and study relationships
reviews.note: Checked each paraphrase against the linked SN 56:11 and SN 22:59 discourses or Bhagavad Gita 2.20, 2.47 and 18.66. Christian claims use the cited Scripture.
